- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downside risk.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean tends to drift above true mean in 30-day horizon; apply a “mean reversion” bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast if recent 10-day average is > 1.5σ above historical mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.5/1.0/0.0), model overfits short-term sentiment; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.25) for 3+ consecutive days, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
